govs.name: Bay County Board of County Commissioners
src: Bay County FY 2026 Final Budget Commissioners' Book (Sept 16, 2025); FY 2026 Final Budget Revenue Detail Report; FY 2026 Final Budget Hearing Presentation
ctx: The countywide general millage stayed at 5.4362 mills for FY2026, the same rate since FY2024. FY2021 through FY2023 used 4.4362 mills; the FY2024 budget raised it by 1.0 mill.
https://www.baycountyfl.gov/Archive.aspx?ADID=313

Commissioners turned down a staff proposal to raise the fire MSTU rate slightly and kept it at 1.38 mills. Part of the cost of new fire apparatus will come from reserves instead, and a Tourist Development Council partnership helps pay for lifeguards.
https://digital-release.mypanhandle.com/news/local-news/bay-county/bay-county-commissioners-approve-2026-budget/amp/

The aggregate adopted rate (6.1067 mills) was 1.81% above the aggregate rolled-back rate (5.9982), so under Florida's TRIM rules it counts as a tax increase even though the millage rates did not change.
https://www.baycountyfl.gov/DocumentCenter/View/18735/FY-2026-Final-Budget-Hearing-Presentation-09-16-2025

The county says roughly $27 million (about 16.5%) of the countywide property taxes it collects goes to Community Redevelopment Agencies run by the cities. That includes an annual payment of about $22.2 million to Panama City Beach's Front Beach Road CRA. The county also says that about 44.7% of its roughly $164 million in General Fund property tax supports the Sheriff, the jail and EMS.
https://www.baycountyfl.gov/829/Understanding-Amendment-3

On a county information page that takes no position, Bay County estimates that statewide Amendment 3 (November 2026 ballot: a larger non-school homestead exemption and a lower assessment cap on non-homestead property) would reduce its recurring revenue by about $22M in FY2027-28 and about $36M in FY2028-29.
https://www.baycountyfl.gov/829/Understanding-Amendment-3
The FY2026 budget adds 25 net new authorized positions: 835 total, up from 810 in FY2025.
https://www.baycountyfl.gov/DocumentCenter/View/18735/FY-2026-Final-Budget-Hearing-Presentation-09-16-2025
The Sheriff is elected separately, but the County Commission pays for most of the office: $74.3M from the county general fund in FY2026 for law enforcement ($43.5M) and the jail ($30.8M).
https://www.baycountyfl.gov/DocumentCenter/View/18382/FY-2026-Final-Budget-Commissioners-Book-09-16-2025
notes: Grouped by researcher from department totals in the FY2026 Final Budget Commissioners' Book General Fund proforma; groups sum to $281,737,981.

src: Bay County FY 2027 Final Budget Hearing Presentation (Sept 23, 2026); FY 2027 Final Budget Detailed Revenues and Expenditures

Amendment 3 on the November 2026 ballot would not change the exemption that applies to school property taxes.
https://floridaphoenix.com/voter-guides/ballot-measures/2026-amendment-3/

gaps: Bay District Schools' final adopted budget for 2025-26 could not be downloaded from the district's site. The total shown is the tentative July 2025 figure, and the fund detail comes from a state education department file.
The school board's split between the state-required rate and the local operating rate is published only as one combined dollar figure ($128.6M).
School rolled-back rates are not published in the state data used here.
The Sheriff's own full budget, including contract and grant money, was not found. The county's link to it opens the Property Appraiser's budget instead. Only the county-funded part is shown.
Callaway, Springfield and Mexico Beach do not post their FY2026 budgets online. Parker posts only a draft. Their tax rates and levies are official.
Where Bay County books its $22.2M Front Beach Road CRA payment is not shown as a line in the county general fund.
Audited figures for FY2025 are not out yet (only Callaway's FY2025 spending has been posted by the state).
Rates for non-ad valorem fees (fire, stormwater, garbage) are incomplete, so the calculator leaves them out.

In the audited figures, CRAs set up as separate legal entities are reported apart from the city or county and are not included here. Bay County's figures include the Sheriff and other constitutional officers but do not split them out.
Tax year 2026 (FY2027) rates had not been published by the state when this page was built.
